Sometime during the exodus from the North Dakota area, Crows acquired the horse (probably from the Shoshoni) and it immediately replaced the dog as a symbol of wealth and prosperity. Following the acquisition of the horse and the whiteman's gun, in the 1730's many rival tribes began migrating into the "Crow Country". Soon inter-tribal conflicts arose and it was not long before warfare became a way of life. According to old tribal historians, there had been little or no serious warfare among the tribes prior to the horse and the gun.
With the newly-acquired means of transportation, the Crows came to depend upon the hunt. This was well suited to their nomadic nature, and allowed them to pursue buffalo herds and defend their vast territory which was virtually surrounded by other enemy tribes. The Crow soon distinguished themselves as competent warriors and were noted among other Plains Tribes for their skillful ability to sneak into enemy camps and ride safely off with stolen horses.
The entire Wolf (Teeth) Mountain range, a former hunting and food gathering area to the south of the Westmoreland Resources lease area, became a buffer zone used by the Crows to defend their shrinking empire against Cheyenne and Sioux war parties coming from the east. Today the hill-top fortifications, lookouts, and temporary camp sites are mute evidence of the buffer zone role played by this area.
